extracted.intended_audience: options exchanges, market data vendors/subscribers, exchange Members and non-Members, and interested persons submitting comments to the SEC on SRO rule filings
extracted.subtask_description: Notice of proposed self-regulatory organization rule changes concerning market-data products and pricing (temporary discount program and market-data product enhancements) published to solicit public comment under the Securities Exchange Act procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary 20% discount program for historical Open-Close Data
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange proposes to provide a temporary 20% discount on fees assessed to Exchange Members and non-Members for any single purchase of End-of-Day Ad-hoc Request (historical data) and/or Intraday ad-hoc Request (historical data) that meets the minimum purchase requirement of at least $20,000 of historical Open-Close Data, effective April 23, 2025 through June 30, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discount applies on an order-by-order basis; orders must contain End-of-Day and/or Intraday Ad-hoc Requests and must total $20,000 or more; the Exchange will not aggregate purchases made throughout a billing cycle for purposes of the incentive program. The discount applies to the total purchase price once the $20,000 minimum is satisfied (example: $25,000 order discounted to $20,000 via 20% discount of $5,000). The program applies to all market participants irrespective of whether they are new or current purchasers, but the discount cannot be combined with any other discounts offered by the Exchange, including the academic discount provided for Qualifying Academic Purchasers of historical Open-Close Data. The Exchange previously adopted the same temporary discount program and is updating dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open-Close Data product definitions and characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: End-of-Day (EOD) Open-Close Data is an end-of-day volume summary of Exchange trading activity at the option level by origin, side of the market, price, and transaction type, with customer and professional customer volume further broken down into trade size buckets. Intraday Open-Close Data provides similar information but is produced and updated every 10 minutes during the trading day (data captured in 10-minute "snapshots" and available to subscribers within five minutes of the conclusion of each 10-minute period). Both are proprietary Exchange historical data products and do not include trade data from other exchanges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EOD is historical, not a real-time feed. Intraday snapshots aggregate current and previous snapshots in each update (example timing: first intraday calculation ~9:42 a.m. ET representing 9:30–9:40 a.m.). These product definitions establish the content and cadence expectations for purchasers and vendors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary nature of Open-Close Data offerings
rubrics_metrics.description: All Open-Close Data products are completely voluntary products; the Exchange is not required by any rule or regulation to make this data available and potential customers may purchase it on an ad-hoc basis only if they voluntarily choose to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customers may purchase on a subscription (monthly/annually) or ad-hoc (historical file for specified month(s)) basis. This voluntariness underpins arguments about competition and non-discriminatory treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum purchase requirement and order aggregation rule
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for the discount an order must contain End-of-Day Ad-hoc Requests and/or Intraday Ad-hoc Requests (historical data) and must total $20,000 or more; the Exchange will not aggregate purchases made throughout a billing cycle for purposes of the incentive program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualification is strictly per-order; purchasers cannot combine multiple smaller orders across a billing cycle to meet the threshold. The guidance includes a numeric example demonstrating discount calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of combination with other discounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The discount cannot be combined with any other discounts offered by the Exchange, including the academic discount provided for Qualifying Academic Purchasers of historical Open-Close Data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants eligible for other discounts must choose treatment; academic discount and the temporary incentive are mutually exclusive for the same purchase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory consistency requirement (Section 6(b) and 6(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange states the proposed rule change is consistent with the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, in particular Section 6(b) and Section 6(b)(5), including that exchange rules be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, promote just and equitable principles of trade, foster cooperation and coordination in processing securities transactions, remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and national market system, protect investors and the public interest, and not be designed to permit unfair discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing must articulate how the proposal furthers these objectives (e.g., expanding data availability, promoting competition, not being unfairly discriminatory). The Exchange uses these statutory touchstones to justify the change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition and substitute-product justification
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange must explain the competitive environment (Open-Close Data is subject to direct competition from similar products offered by other options exchanges) and identify substitute products (examples provided: Nasdaq PHLX Options Trade Outline, ISE Profile, GEMX Trade Profile, open-close data from C2, Cboe Options, BZX, MIAX, Pearl, Emerald, NYSE Options Open-Close Volume Summary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing argues that competitive forces constrain fees and that purchasers may switch to alternatives; the presence of substitutes supports the claim that fees and discounts are competitive rather than anticompetitive. Market-share context (no single exchange has >17% market share) and Regulation NMS precedent are used to support the competitive rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self‑Regulatory Organization’s statement on burden on competition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange must state whether the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act, and explain why it does or does not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical justifications include: operating in a highly competitive environment, competitors free to modify fees in response, presence of substitute products, optional nature of data purchases, and uniform application of the incentive (applies to any purchaser who meets minimum). The Exchange explains why the proposal permits fair competition among national securities exchanges and will not cause unnecessary or inappropriate burdens on intermarket competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation of comments procedures and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the proposed rule change, including whether it is consistent with the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments may be submitted electronically via the Commission’s internet comment form or email (include file number SR‑CboeEDGX‑2025‑036 or relevant file number), or as paper comments in triplicate to the SEC Secretary. All submissions should refer to the file number and be submitted by the stated deadline (e.g., on or before June 12, 2025). Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; the SEC may redact or withhold obscene or copyrighted material. The Commission will post all comments on its website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and inspection of filings and related communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of the submission, subsequent amendments, written statements, and communications relating to the proposed rule change will be available for website viewing and printing on the Commission’s internet website and for inspection and copying at the Exchange’s principal office and the Commission’s Public Reference Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public Reference Room hours (official business days between 10 a.m. and 3 p.m.) are provided. The filing text is also available on the Exchange’s website.

rubrics_metrics.name: NYSE Texas Aggregated Lite product specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: NYSE Texas Aggregated Lite is a NYSE Texas‑only frequency‑based depth-of-book market data feed of the Exchange’s limit order book for up to ten (10) price levels; updated no less frequently than once per second; includes depth of book order data and security status messages (trading halts, short sale restrictions, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing explains content and update cadence expectations for the product and that it is a compilation provided to vendors and subscribers. References to related prior filings and affiliate product parity are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Auction Imbalance Information in Aggregated Lite
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange proposes to include Auction Imbalance Information in the NYSE Texas Aggregated Lite product in connection with the introduction of auctions on NYSE Texas. Auction Imbalance Information includes, if applicable, the Total Imbalance, Market Imbalance, Indicative Match Price and Matched Volume (as defined in NYSE Texas Rule 7.35(a)), and real-time order imbalances that accumulate prior to the opening, prior to re-opening after a halt, and prior to the close.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The enhanced feed would contain aggregate information about orders subject to execution at opening or closing prices and would provide Auction Imbalance Information with respect to all symbols listed on the Exchange. The Exchange will announce availability via a Trader Update.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced Aggregated Lite product availability and nondiscrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: The enhanced NYSE Texas Aggregated Lite market data product would be available to all of the Exchange’s vendors and subscribers on an equivalent basis at no cost (the Exchange currently does not charge a fee for subscribing to the feed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing states this availability supports the claim that the proposal would not permit unfair discrimination. Comparisons to affiliate feeds (NYSE, NYSE Arca, NYSE American) and Nasdaq are provided to show parity with other exchanges' offerings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of NYSE Texas Order Imbalances proprietary product
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange proposes to establish the NYSE Texas Order Imbalances product as a separate, stand‑alone real‑time market data feed of information the Exchange would provide in advance of an auction: real-time order imbalances that accumulate prior to the opening, prior to any re-opening auction after a halt, and prior to the close of trading, containing aggregate information about orders subject to execution at the market’s opening or closing price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The product is tied to the introduction of auctions (see proposed Rule 7.35) and mirrors the auction-related imbalance information described for Aggregated Lite but as a distinct proprietary feed. The filing situates the product among other real‑time imbalance feeds and emphasizes the product content and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness filing route and Rule 19b‑4(f)(6) waiver criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange filed certain proposed rule changes pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) and Rule 19b‑4(f)(6). A proposed rule change filed under Rule 19b‑4(f)(6) normally does not become operative prior to 30 days after filing, but the Commission may waive that delay if the proposal does not (i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) impose any significant burden on competition; and (iii) become operative prior to 30 days from filing, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, if consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange requested waiver of the 30‑day operative delay to implement changes as soon as technology is available; the Commission considers impact on efficiency, competition, and capital formation when waiving the delay and may designate the proposal operative upon filing if consistent with investor protection and the public interest.
